title.narrative: NICFI 26-28 - Utviklingsfondet - Imprvd rights, livelihoods & forest mgmt

description.narrative:
The project is in many ways a continuation of the Development Fund's (DF) project in Ethiopia supported by Norad since 2013 (ETH-21/0003) and Norwegian Church Aid's (NCA) project (ETH-21/0006) supported by Norad since 2021.
The project aims to reduce deforestation in southwest Ethiopia (the South West Forest Block being the largest intact tropical forest area in Ethiopia), by strengthening land rights and recognition of Participatory Forest Management (PFM) institutions and faith-based structures in target areas, as well as establishing sustainable livelihood models that prevent further forest encroachment. The project builds on the use of PFM-methodology, a step-wise methodology that involves the local population in the formal management of the forest and forest resources.
Project outcomes are: Outcome 1: Local communities and faith-based structures in targeted areas have strengthened rights, and their contribution to sustainable forest management, reduced deforestation and conservation of biodiversity is recognised. Outcome 2: Households in targeted forest dependent communities have improved livelihoods through diversified forest friendly livelihood options.
The project will be managed by a consortium led by DF and NCA. The Ethio-Wetlands and Natural Resource Associaton (EWNRA) is DF's main implementing partner and is responsible for implementation of the PFM methodology. The International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) will support the project by enabling Global South–South learning, citizen-led forest research and mapping, and inclusive forest governance through capacity building. NCA will continue to work with their current implementing partners of faith-based institutions (ECO-DIAC, EMRDA, EECMY-DASSC). They will also work with their well-known scientific and technical partner CIFOR-ICRAF.
The project doucmentation shows an intentional effort toward gender equality, with clear ambitions and follow-up measures.
